name: casimir_su
statement: Let $N \ge 2$ and let $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ be the real Lie algebra of traceless skew-Hermitian $N \times N$ complex matrices, with the inner product $\langle X, Y\rangle = -\frac{1}{N}\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(XY)$. Let $K(X,Y)$ be the Killing form of $\mathfrak{su}(N)$, the trace of the real-linear map $Z \mapsto [X,[Y,Z]]$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Prove that $K(X,Y) = 2N\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ for all $X, Y \in \mathfrak{su}(N)$, so that $K(X,Y) = -C\langle X, Y\rangle$ with $C = 2N^2$.

name: trace_ad_ad
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $N$ a natural number. For $N \times N$ matrices $A, B$ over $R$, the $R$-linear map $Z \mapsto AZB$ on the $N \times N$ matrices has trace $\operatorname{tr}(A)\operatorname{tr}(B)$. Prove that, for $N \times N$ matrices $X, Y$ over $R$, the trace of the $R$-linear map $Z \mapsto [X,[Y,Z]]$ on the $N \times N$ matrices equals $2N\operatorname{tr}(XY) - 2\operatorname{tr}(X)\operatorname{tr}(Y)$.

name: purity_bounds
statement: Let $(\lambda_j)_{j \ge 1}$ be a summable sequence of real numbers with $\lambda_1 > 0$ and $0 \le \lambda_j \le \lambda_1$ for all $j$, and let $n \ge 1$ be an integer. Put $Z(m) = \sum_{j \ge 1} \lambda_j^m$, $r_j = (\lambda_j/\lambda_1)^n$, $s_n = \sum_{j \ge 2} r_j$, $q_n = \sum_{j \ge 2} r_j^2$ and $P(n) = Z(2n)/Z(n)^2$. Prove that $P(n) = \frac{1+q_n}{(1+s_n)^2} \le 1$, that $s_n \le \frac{1}{P(n)} - 1 \le 2s_n + s_n^2$, and that $s_{2n} \le s_n^2$, where $s_{2n} = \sum_{j \ge 2} (\lambda_j/\lambda_1)^{2n}$.

name: gap_from_purity
statement: Let $(\lambda_j)_{j \ge 1}$ be a summable sequence of real numbers with $\lambda_1 > 0$, $\lambda_2 > 0$ and $0 \le \lambda_j \le \lambda_1$ for all $j$, and let $n \ge 1$ be an integer. Put $Z(m) = \sum_{j \ge 1} \lambda_j^m$, $P(n) = Z(2n)/Z(n)^2$ and $\mathsf{m} = \log(\lambda_1/\lambda_2)$. Prove that $e^{-n\mathsf{m}} \le \frac{1}{P(n)} - 1$, and that if $P(n) > \frac12$ then $\mathsf{m} \ge \frac1n \log \frac{1}{P(n)^{-1} - 1}$.

name: defect_telescope
statement: Let $z_1, z_2, z_3, z_4, z_5$ be positive real numbers, and put $P_1 = z_2/z_1^2$, $P_2 = z_3/z_2^2$, $P_3 = z_4/z_3^2$, $P_4 = z_5/z_4^2$ and $\Delta = 16\log z_1 - \log z_5$. Assume $P_k \le 1$ for $k = 1, 2, 3, 4$. Prove that $e^{-\Delta} = P_1^8 P_2^4 P_3^2 P_4$, that $\Delta \ge 0$, and that $P_4 \ge e^{-\Delta}$.

name: gap_from_defect
statement: Let $(\lambda_j)_{j \ge 1}$ be a summable sequence of real numbers with $\lambda_1 > 0$, $\lambda_2 > 0$ and $0 \le \lambda_j \le \lambda_1$ for all $j$, and let $n \ge 1$ be an integer. Put $Z(m) = \sum_{j \ge 1} \lambda_j^m$ and $P(n) = Z(2n)/Z(n)^2$. Let $\Delta$ be a real number with $0 < \Delta < \log 2$ and $P(n) \ge e^{-\Delta}$. Prove that $\log(\lambda_1/\lambda_2) \ge \frac1n \log \frac{1}{e^{\Delta} - 1}$.

name: conditional_gap
statement: Let $c_1 \ge 2$ be a real number and $n \ge 1$ an integer. Let $(\delta_k)_{k \ge 0}$ be positive real numbers with $\delta_0 \le \frac{1}{2c_1}$ such that, for every $k$, $\delta_k \le \frac{1}{2c_1}$ implies $\delta_{k+1} \le c_1\delta_k^2$. Let $(m_k)_{k \ge 0}$ be real numbers with $m_k \ge \frac{1}{2^k n}\log\frac{1}{e^{\delta_k} - 1}$ for every $k$. Prove that $m_k \ge \frac{\log 2}{n}$ for every $k$.
